title: Plan three meals that share ingredients without wasting them

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: A shopping plan starts with usable quantities and actual storage, not package count. A cheap item that cannot be used or stored is not automatically a saving. Follow the relevant product and local food-safety instructions in a real kitchen.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Complete fictional three-meal unit for one adult with confirmed suitable diet and equipment: each meal uses one 250 g ready-to-use bean portion, one 200 g vegetable portion and one bread portion. Inventory: beans 250 g, vegetables 400 g, bread 1 portion, all within labeled use/storage conditions. Prices: beans 250 g=2 units, vegetables 200 g=1, bread 2 portions=2. Budget 8. Fridge space fits one vegetable portion; unopened beans/bread follow their labels. No extra food need or nutrition claim is supplied.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Calculate total requirements, subtract usable stock, price the gaps and choose a storage-feasible list. If vegetables are unavailable, the shop offers an equally suitable 200 g alternative for 2 units.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A two-portion pack costs 3 units; a five-portion pack costs 6 but only two portions can be used or safely stored. Which comparison matters?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: Require 750 g beans,600 g vegetables,3 bread portions. Buy beans 500 g=4, vegetables 200 g=1, bread 2=2: total 7, leaving 1. Alternative vegetables raise total to 8. Partial: correct costs but buy all requirements again. Incorrect: call a bulk bargain usable without storage or invent dietary suitability beyond the case. Actual shopping and food handling remain unperformed.
criteria: Inventory is subtracted in compatible units
Budget and storage both constrain the list

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: The smaller pack costs 3 for the two usable portions; the larger costs 6 for the same usable outcome with three unallocated portions. Unit price alone does not establish value; a real sharing/storage option would need confirmation.
